lines.text: What happens if your elevator snaps and plunges into a freefall?
Most people believe jumping right before impact will cancel the speed and save you.
But physics says this is completely impossible.
The elevator is falling at fifty miles an hour, while you can only jump up at two miles an hour.
Plus, jumping up will slam your head directly into the descending ceiling.
If you try standing with bent knees, the sheer G force will snap your legs and shatter your spine.
The only real way to survive is to lie flat on your back in the center of the floor.
This spreads the catastrophic impact evenly across your entire body and shields your vital organs.
Never jump in an elevator, always lie flat.
